description:
Problem: when develop's base itself is invalid, no PR can pass a required check. That happened on 2026-10-24, when a comment-policy scope entry named a missing file. The only recovery was the owner removing one required context from ruleset 15611785 for one merge and restoring it. No document describes this procedure: develop 9a184b619 has no break-glass text in docs/agent/merge-authority.md, docs/internal/merge-queue-governance.md or docs/internal/repo-admin-settings.md. Nothing checks that the restore was complete, including each context's integration_id binding.

Outcome: a written owner procedure, and a read-back command that proves the ruleset matches its pre-relaxation capture.

Decision gates:
1. Owner-only execution. Agents never edit rulesets. This item writes the procedure and the verification command; running the relaxation stays an owner action.
2. Automatic recovery. Advisor prevention row 2 proposes trusted checker logic that recovers from a paired notice/selector relocation by itself. Decide whether to build it and record the decision with its reason. Default: no. It is new trusted logic, it must be installed before the next incident to help at all, and the break-glass procedure covers today's frequency. If the owner wants it, file a separate item.
3. Comparison source. Extend scripts/ruleset_drift_check.py rather than adding a parallel script, unless its structure makes a before/after comparison impossible; record why if so.

The procedure covers: one named PR and head SHA; holds on competing armed PRs; a full ruleset JSON capture before the change; removal of exactly one context; the merge; immediate restore on success or failure; a full read-back compared to the capture; and confirmation of oracle-gate integration 5201041 and every other context's binding, with timestamps.

Item guardrails: no ruleset edits by agents, including in tests; tests use captured JSON fixtures only.

Common guardrails: work only in a linked worktree created by make worktree-create, after make agent-write-preflight; the primary clone is read-only. No SKIP or --no-verify, no stand-in approvals, no ruleset edits or bypasses, no raw gh pr merge. Do not close and reopen, mass-rerun or rebase other pull requests.
